earlier_scan.source_named: Westermann, Diedrich 1933. Grammar sketch covering Bago (Drei Dialekte des Tem in Togo: Cala, Delo und Bago, MSOS). Glottolog med ref 118962; not accessible online.

new_statements.quote: The language contrasts two levels of tone: high and low. In the transcription, a high tone is marked by an acute accent, and a low tone is unmarked. Lexically, tone plays an important role in determining the meaning of a word. The following pairs differ in their meanings solely as a result of their tonal patterns. [p. 47] ... In addition to the two levels, a contour tone is formed only in a heavy syllable. A falling or a raising contour is never found on a short vowel. A nasal segment is a tone-bearing unit, as in many Niger-Congo languages [...]. Following Yip's (2002) distinction between moraic and syllabic tone-bearing units, this thesis considers the mora as the tone-bearing unit in Bago. [p. 48]
new_statements.citation: Alansary, Emad (2021). Topics in the Grammar of Bago. MA thesis, University of Ottawa. DOI 10.20381/ruor-27263

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bago is a two-tone (H/L) register-tone language with lexically contrastive tone, contour tones restricted to bimoraic syllables and the mora as tone-bearing unit. The source makes no statement about word stress at all (the words 'stress', 'stressed', 'prominence' do not occur in the 399-page thesis); no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal: only two tonal rules (finite-verb formation, number-suffixation); HL pattern absent from infinitives; long vowels in verbs always carry a single level tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone description (nouns, verbs, suffixes); citation-form elicitation from one main Kusuntu-born consultant speaking Bago plus recorded texts. Describes the Bago variety, not Kusuntu.
new_statements.identity_note: Alansary 2021 describes the Bago variety (main consultant a native Kusuntu speaker fluent in Bago); Ethnologue/Glottolog treat Bago and Kusuntu as dialects of bago1245 [bqg], while Kleinewillinghöfer 2000, Moussa 2011 and Takougnandi 2016 treat them as closely related distinct languages (Alansary 2021: 6). The tone statement applies to Bago; nothing was opened for Kusuntu.

sources.note: Nothing: 'stress/stressed/prominence' never occur (grep = 0 hits). Ch. 2 (pp. 17-56) gives consonants, vowels, vowel length/harmony, syllable structure and a tone section 2.4 (pp. 47-56): two level tones H and L, lexically contrastive; contour tones only on heavy syllables (long vowels, nasal codas); mora = tone-bearing unit; tone rules in finite-verb formation and number suffixation. Describes the Bago variety (consultant a Kusuntu native who speaks Bago); author treats Bago and Kusuntu as closely related but distinct (p. 6).
